messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: Aroma.affymetrix package: annotate copy number estimate with SNPs and Gene names
parts:
Hi.

On Thu, Jan 13, 2011 at 8:56 PM, Zhu, Lihua (Julie)
<Juli...@umassmed.edu> wrote:
> Henrik,
>
> Thanks so much for developing such a useful package!
>
> I have followed the instructions on http://www.aroma-project.org/.
>
> A list of copy numbers for all samples and units were generated. Now I want
> to annotate the copy number estimate C with SNPs and gene names. Could you
> please shed some light on how to proceed?
>
> theta.ALL.BCR.ABL <- do.call(cbind, lapply(1:length(cesN$Names),
> function(i){
>    ce <- getFile(cesN, i)
>    theta <- extractTheta(ce)
> }
> ))

Instead of doing the above, just do:

theta.ALL.BCR.ABL <- extractTheta(cesN, drop=TRUE);

(assuming that you are doing total CN analysis, i.e. combineAlleles=TRUE.)

> ceR <- getAverageFile(cesN.r, verbose=verbose)
> thetaR <- extractTheta(ceR)
> thetaR = as.vector(thetaR)

Instead, just do:

thetaR <- extractTheta(ceR, drop=TRUE);

> C <- 2*theta.ALL.BCR.ABL/thetaR

To add the CDF unit names as rownames, just do:

unf <- getUnitNamesFile(cesN); # This will for Affymetrix be the CDF
rownames(C) <- getUnitNames(unf);

which gives:

print(C[2001:2003,1:4]);
GSM226867 GSM226868 GSM226869 GSM226870
SNP_A-1512786 2.009220 2.438844 1.889013 1.782385
SNP_A-1512840 1.149404 1.741206 1.759043 2.096061
SNP_A-1513972 2.038601 2.077377 1.623648 1.530445

Hope this helps

/Henrik

>
> Thanks so much for your kind help!
>
> Best regards,
>
> Julie

parts:
Hi.

On Fri, Jan 14, 2011 at 3:34 PM, Zhu, Lihua (Julie)
<Juli...@umassmed.edu> wrote:
> Henrik,
>
> Thanks so much for the detailed response! It is very helpful!
>
> I have a few additional questions.
>
> 1. Is there a function to convert the unit name to gene name and SNP name?

I'd use the biomaRt package for that; please use the Bioconductor
resources for that.

> 2. Is there a function to detect copy number variation using circular binary
> segmentation or other segmentation algorithms?

Yes. For instance, see the end of the 'Paired total copy-number
analysis' vignette:

http://aroma-project.org/vignettes/pairedTotalCopyNumberAnalysis

If you don't have paired arrays, the do something like:

cbs <- CbsModel(cesN);
fit(cbs, arrays=1:4, chromosomes=c(4,6:9,15), verbose=TRUE);

...

> 3. Any downstream analysis functions are available in aroma or other
> packages I should use?

The Aroma framework provides methods up to segmentation. After that,
please turn to other resources, cf. Bioconductor.

Also, if you don't find documentation on the website, make sure search
the mailing list archives, because many questions have already been
answered there: http://aroma-project.org/forum

Cheers,

/Henrik

>
> Thanks so much for your kind help!

> Best regards,
>
> Julie
